svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS shipped two products that made an application a first-class object and has withdrawn both. AWS Service Catalog AppRegistry is transitioning to maintenance mode and is no longer open to new customers from July 30 2026, with no new features and no expansion into new AWS Regions. myApplications no longer allows creation of new applications or updates of existing applications, though existing users may continue to access and view previously created ones. Underneath, an application consisted of four parts and three of them survive the withdrawal. The application object itself is withdrawn. The awsApplication tag survives and persists indefinitely: it is an ordinary user tag whose value is a Resource Groups ARN of the form arn:aws:resource-groups:us-east-1:234567891011:group/myExampleApp/012345example6789101112131. The resource groups survive, because AWS Resource Groups creates an application group plus one group for every CloudFormation stack or tag-based resource associated with the application. Attribute groups, which are JSON documents of application metadata shared across applications, remain reachable only through the frozen products and have no direct replacement. Membership always followed the tag rather than the application object, since any resource tagged with the awsApplication tag for an application is a member of its group, and the tag could always be written with ordinary tagging methods or infrastructure as code. That is why AWS can say no action is required and that resources retain the tag. AWS names a replacement per use case: tagging with a key you choose for metadata, AWS Resource Groups for organisation, AWS Resource Explorer for discovery, all three at no additional cost, and CloudWatch Application Signals for observability as a paid service with a free tier. There is no mandated tag key, with application, project and workload offered as common conventions. On quotas, the product allowed 2,000 applications per Region at 1,000 resources each, a documented ceiling of 2,000,000 resource associations in one Region, but the limit that actually binds is 100 resource groups per account in each Region, which the product-created groups consume, and the awsApplication tag occupies one of the 50 user tags a resource is allowed, leaving 49.
svg.title: The abstraction was withdrawn twice; the tag underneath it persists
svg.text: Two abstractions withdrawn. The tag underneath them persists indefinitely.
“No action is required. Resources … retain the awsApplication tag and remain accessible through tools like AWS Resource Groups.”
SERVICE CATALOG APPREGISTRY
“transitioning to maintenance mode … no longer
be open to new customers starting July 30, 2026”
No new features. No new Regions.
MYAPPLICATIONS
“no longer allows creation of new applications
or updates of existing applications”
Existing ones are read-only now.
What an application was made of — three of the four parts survive
the application object WITHDRAWN — the only part that pointed at the others
awsApplication tag SURVIVES — a user tag, “persists indefinitely”
the resource groups SURVIVE — one per application, plus one per stack
attribute groups shared JSON metadata — no direct replacement
The tag value is not a name. It is a resource group ARN.
awsApplication = arn:aws:resource-groups:us-east-1:234567891011:group/myExampleApp/012345example6789101112131
What AWS names instead, one destination per use case
metadata tagging, with a key you choose no additional cost
organisation AWS Resource Groups (#106) no additional cost
discovery AWS Resource Explorer (#105) no additional cost
observability → CloudWatch
Application Signals, the one
that is not free.
The quota that actually binds
Not 2,000 applications or 1,000 resources each.
100 resource groups per account, per Region —
and the product-created ones count.
Pick the key yourself now
“There is no single mandated tag key … Common
conventions include application, project, or workload.”
One of your 50 user tags is already spoken for.
This abstraction added a lookup, not a capability — so it is the part that could be withdrawn.
The durable artefact is a tag key you chose, applied consistently, defended by a policy, and queried by a group you can account for.
